required_fixes: Add an explicit statement that the sustainability-related financial disclosures are for the same reporting entity as the related financial statements (boundary alignment) (IFRS_S1_20_C01).

Identify the specific related financial statements to which these sustainability-related financial disclosures relate (eg, consolidated financial statements for year ended 31 Dec 2024) (IFRS_S1_22_C01).
Add explicit linkage that the reporting currency used (EUR) is the presentation currency of the related financial statements (IFRS_S1_24_C01).
Add an explicit statement about consistency (to the extent possible) of data and assumptions with those used in the related financial statements (IFRS_S1_23_C01).

Describe connections across sustainability disclosures and other general purpose financial reports (eg, where in the financial statements related impacts/amounts are reflected, or provide cross-references) (IFRS_S1_21_C04).
Disclose the specific standards/guidance applied (eg, IFRS S1, IFRS S2, NGFS scenarios, GHG Protocol, PCAF) and, if applicable, SASB disclosure topics considered (IFRS_S1_59_C01).
Disclose whether and how SASB Standards were considered for applicability (topics and, where relevant, metrics), or state they were assessed as not applicable (IFRS_S1_55_C01, IFRS_S1_58_C01).

Clarify the basis for identifying applicable disclosure requirements for each material sustainability-related risk/opportunity (apply specifically applicable IFRS SDS; and where none exists, disclose the judgement framework used) (IFRS_S1_56_C01, IFRS_S1_57_C01, IFRS_S1_57_C02).

Strengthen the scope statement to address 'all sustainability-related risks and opportunities' (not only climate) or clearly scope the section as climate-only and ensure the overall report covers all material sustainability topics (IFRS_S1_3_C01).
State whether the sustainability-related financial disclosures are issued at the same time as the related financial statements (IFRS_S1_64_C01).

Add/attach the missing evidence items (or cite them explicitly in the evidence pack) for: metadata.comparative_years, reporting_kpis.financed_emissions_2024_tco2e, governance[*] fields (board size, expertise %, agenda %, committee cadence, committee names), metadata.risk_rating_methodology, metadata.scope2_rec_reconciliation, metadata.pcaf_methodology.sovereign_bonds_note, reporting_kpis emissions data quality breakdown, reporting_kpis external assurance level, financial_summary tier 1 and climate capex values, value_chain_map node and scope 3 travel KPI, and scope 1/2 KPI values.

If quantitative evidence cannot be provided for certain narrative assertions (e.g., 'adequate resilience', 'within Pillar 2 thresholds'), qualify the language (e.g., 'management assessment') and/or add the underlying quantitative results/thresholds and definitions.
For statements implying trends (e.g., 'rising acute physical risk'), either provide supporting trend evidence (time series/analysis) or rephrase to avoid asserting a trend.

Remove or generalize hard-coded reporting years, specific dates, currencies, and detailed numeric values from this general requirements template section, or clearly frame them as current-period facts that are expected to change each reporting cycle; ensure this aligns with the 'what to avoid' list for this section.
Add a one-sentence purpose statement at the start of each subsection (1.1–1.9) that explains the objective of the subsection and how it helps users interpret the disclosures.

Introduce explicit IFRS pillar subheadings or cross-references (Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics and Targets) where relevant content is discussed, especially within the 'Connected information' and methodology subsections.

Apply the layered structure more consistently: start with an overview sentence, follow with bullets or (where appropriate) a compact table, and close with a short connectivity sentence that references related sections (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Governance]' or 'See [Section: Metrics and Targets]').
Shorten or split long sentences, particularly in the scenario analysis and resilience assessment paragraphs, to improve clarity and align with the sentence length guidance.
Define acronyms and technical terms (e.g., NGFS, IEA, NACE, EPC, CDP, EVIC) at first use in this section or cross-reference to a definitions/appendix section.

Increase use of preferred standards-oriented verbs and active voice for the reporting entity (e.g., 'we prepare', 'we disclose', 'we assess', 'we monitor') while keeping third-person or passive voice for externally defined requirements.

Consider introducing at least one or two compact tables with captions (e.g., a table summarizing the risk rating bands and another summarizing emissions data quality categories) to improve scanability and align with table usage and evidence/traceability rules.
Add brief closing sentences to major subsections that explicitly link the content to other parts of the report or financial statements using generic cross-reference placeholders.

Review the section for any residual narrative or descriptive phrasing that could be made more process- and control-focused, emphasizing how information is prepared, assessed, and monitored rather than characterizing performance.

approval_policy: V9.0 approves sections that pass deterministic/fact-lock gates and meet supported-evidence-scope judge thresholds; missing requirements remain audit-only.

section_generation_score.policy: Missing requirements reduce audit/readiness visibility only; they must not appear in report prose.
